migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC migration programme governance, inventory all device models, firmware versions, cryptographic libraries, and cloud endpoints; define cryptographic bill of materials (CBOM).
prerequisites: Access to firmware source repositories and device fleet inventory
Cloud architecture documentation from AWS account

migration_steps.activity: Profile memory, flash, CPU, and power budgets on representative devices (thermostat, camera, door lock) for ECC P-256 baseline and candidate PQC algorithms; measure ML-KEM and ML-DSA stack/heap and code size using reference implementations.
prerequisites: Hardware development kits and debug probes available
Reference PQC implementations (e.g., NIST FIPS 203/204 reference code) obtained

migration_steps.activity: Evaluate hybrid and PQC-only TLS 1.2/1.3 options for constrained devices; assess ML-KEM-512/768 and ML-DSA-44/65 memory footprints against 64KB RAM and 256KB flash; determine feasibility of secure boot with ML-DSA versus hybrid ECDSA+ML-DSA.
prerequisites: TLS library vendor roadmaps (e.g., mbedTLS, wolfSSL) obtained

migration_steps.activity: Select target cryptographic architecture: hybrid key establishment (ECDHE P-256 + ML-KEM) for TLS, and hybrid or ML-DSA-only secure boot depending on flash budget; document algorithm roles and fallback policy.
prerequisites: Risk acceptance criteria approved by product security board

migration_steps.activity: Engage silicon vendor, TLS library vendor, and AWS to confirm PQC support timelines, memory requirements, and certification implications; obtain written roadmaps and support statements.
Develop and unit-test PQC integration in a non-production firmware branch: integrate ML-KEM and ML-DSA into TLS stack and secure boot chain; run on emulator and hardware development kits.
prerequisites: Step 5 vendor support confirmations for library versions

migration_steps.activity: Conduct performance, memory, and power regression testing on all device classes; validate secure boot with PQC signatures and TLS handshake with hybrid key exchange; document resource headroom.
prerequisites: Test harness and device farm available

migration_steps.activity: Perform security review and threat modelling of PQC integration; assess side-channel resistance, key storage, and downgrade attack resistance; obtain internal security sign-off.
Prepare cloud backend for PQC: enable hybrid TLS termination on AWS load balancers/CloudFront where supported; plan for ML-KEM support expected in 2027; implement crypto-agility in backend services.
prerequisites: Backend change approval outside freeze windows

migration_steps.activity: Plan and execute pilot deployment to a limited fleet (e.g., internal test devices and beta customers) during allowed change windows, avoiding Nov 15–Jan 15 freeze; monitor for interoperability and performance issues.
prerequisites: Step 9 cloud hybrid TLS enabled in staging

migration_steps.activity: Stage production firmware rollout in phases across device models, respecting change freeze; maintain ECC fallback for legacy cloud endpoints until AWS ML-KEM support is confirmed and validated.
prerequisites: AWS ML-KEM production support confirmed and tested (expected 2027, unconfirmed)

migration_steps.activity: Complete migration to ML-KEM for key establishment and ML-DSA for secure boot where feasible; decommission ECC-only paths after validation; update CBOM and documentation.
prerequisites: AWS ML-KEM support validated in production

blockers.blocker: ML-KEM and ML-DSA memory footprint may exceed 64KB RAM / 256KB flash on constrained devices.
blockers.reason: NIST PQC algorithms require larger keys, ciphertexts, and code size than ECC P-256; secure boot with ML-DSA may not fit alongside application firmware.
blockers.resolution_required: Complete Step 2 profiling; if infeasible, adopt hybrid approach with ML-KEM only for TLS and retain ECDSA for secure boot until hardware refresh, or select devices with larger memory for PQC-capable firmware.

blockers.blocker: AWS ML-KEM support is forecast for 2027 but not confirmed as available or validated.
blockers.reason: Cloud backend cannot negotiate ML-KEM until AWS provides production support; presenting it as available would be an unconfirmed dependency.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written AWS roadmap and support commitment; validate in staging once available; maintain hybrid ECDHE fallback until confirmed.

blockers.blocker: TLS library and silicon vendor PQC support status unconfirmed.
blockers.reason: Embedded TLS stacks (e.g., mbedTLS, wolfSSL) and hardware crypto accelerators may not yet support ML-KEM/ML-DSA with acceptable memory footprint.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain vendor roadmaps and support statements (Step 5); require evidence of tested PQC builds for the specific MCU family.

blockers.blocker: Change freeze from Nov 15 to Jan 15 restricts production changes.
blockers.reason: Production firmware and cloud changes cannot be deployed during freeze; scheduling must avoid this window.
blockers.resolution_required: Schedule all production changes outside freeze; use freeze period for non-production testing and planning only if permitted by change policy.

blockers.blocker: Secure boot and TLS changes may require recertification (e.g., PSA Certified, FCC, industry compliance).
blockers.reason: PQC algorithm changes alter cryptographic module boundaries and may invalidate existing certifications.
blockers.resolution_required: Identify certification impact in Step 3; engage certification bodies early; budget for recertification.

blockers.blocker: Budget of $150,000 may be insufficient for full PQC migration including hardware refresh and certification.
blockers.reason: PQC integration, testing, certification, and potential hardware changes can exceed budget.
blockers.resolution_required: Prioritise hybrid TLS and secure boot feasibility; defer full ML-DSA secure boot if memory-constrained; seek additional budget if certification costs exceed allocation.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Forecast: ML-KEM support expected in 2027; not confirmed as available or validated.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Written AWS roadmap and service-specific support statement; staging validation results for hybrid TLS with ML-KEM.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Unconfirmed; PQC support may be in development or limited to larger platforms.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Vendor roadmap, memory footprint benchmarks for ML-KEM/ML-DSA on target MCU, and test reports.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Unconfirmed; hardware crypto acceleration for PQC may not be available.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Datasheet or support statement confirming PQC acceleration or sufficient resources; reference implementation performance data.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Unconfirmed; PQC algorithm changes may require new certification.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Certification requirements and timeline for PQC-modified firmware; formal approval.

algorithm_roles.ML-KEM: Post-quantum key establishment for TLS 1.2/1.3 between devices and cloud; used in hybrid mode with ECDHE P-256 during transition; not used for digital signatures.
algorithm_roles.ML-DSA: Post-quantum digital signatures for secure boot and firmware authentication; used where flash memory permits; may be deferred or hybridised with ECDSA on constrained devices.

cost_assumptions.category: Vendor support and licensing (TLS library, tools)

raw_response.confidence: Medium: technical feasibility and vendor timelines (especially AWS ML-KEM in 2027) are unconfirmed; memory constraints may force hybrid or deferred ML-DSA secure boot; budget is tight but within limit under stated assumptions.
